idea: Themed weeks, week four, Money day: written from the source, then corrected by a numbers editor and a viewer editor before voicing.
description: Women were 36.1% of Odisha's Atal Pension Yojana enrolments in 2015-16 (39,987 of 110,846 women and men) and 67.2% in 2024-25 (307,791 of 458,317), a rise of 31.1 points. Women's enrolments multiplied 7.7 times in nine years; men's, 2.1 times. Women were more than half of Odisha's enrolees in each of the last four years.

In 2024-25 fewer men enrolled than the year before, 187,494 down to 150,526, a fall of 20%; women's enrolments also rose, 265,290 to 307,791, so both moved the share. A Lok Sabha answer gives 66.5% for Odisha in 2024-25 (India 54.6%) and 63.4% for 2025-26 to 31 January. The map is blank for 18 states and UTs where the Handbook's counts differ from that answer or the boundary changed; they are named in the source. Enrolments in a year; transgender enrolments are left out of the share.
source: PFRDA Handbook of NPS Statistics 2024, via RBI Handbook of Statistics on Indian States 2024-25, Table 180: Atal Pension Yojana enrolments in the year; share = women ÷ (women + men), transgender left out. Also Lok Sabha answer 2656, 9 Mar 2026. Blank on the map (counts differ from that answer, or boundary changed): Andaman and Nicobar, Arunachal Pradesh, Chandigarh, Chhattisgarh, Dadra-Daman-Diu, Delhi, Goa, J&K, Karnataka, Kerala, Lakshadweep, Maharashtra, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim, Telangana. Ladakh is not in the table.

done: Numbers editor recomputed from Table 180 and checked it against RBI's own table page (dated 11 Dec 2025): Odisha 2015-16 women 39,987, men 70,859; 2024-25 women 3,07,791, men 1,50,526; share 36.07% and 67.16%; shares by year 36.1, 35.5, 43.1, 50.2, 50.4, 50.3, 52.4, 56.0, 58.6, 67.2.

Compared all 35 Handbook rows for 2022-23 to 2024-25 and the ten-year total against Lok Sabha Q 2656 (9 Mar 2026, Annexures I and II, read in the PDF). Odisha agrees (Handbook totals 0.94 to 0.97 of the answer's; shares within 0.7 points); 17 states pass the rule and are shown, 18 are blank (the rule and the 18 names are in the source line).

Fixed before voicing: 'half or more in each of the last seven years' became 'more than half in each of the last four' (2018-19 to 2020-21 cannot be cross-checked); men's fall of 20% got its own card; the Lok Sabha figures (66.5%, 63.4%, India 54.6%) are on screen beside the Handbook's 67%. Viewer editor put the scheme name in the voice and changed the closing question to 'Have you started a pension?' (the old one could not be answered from a half-blank map).

Claude checked every figure quoted in this pack's description, Instagram text, X post and pinned comment against the built data.json (screen text, voice lines and the builder's own checks); none is new.
